images.title: Same centre, different spread
images.purpose: Recap how to describe two groups: read the extremes and range first, then the centre, using two groups with the same mean but different spreads.
images.composition: Two short dot plots, Group A above Group B, on one scale, with one dashed mean line through both and a range bracket under each.
exact_structure: Two dark grey (#2B2B2B) number lines from 0 to 20, one above the other and aligned, each with 21 small ticks, one at every whole number; only the bottom line has numbered ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20.
Top line, labelled Group A: 5 teal (#0072B2) dots at 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12; under it a teal bracket from 8 to 12 labelled Range = 4.
Bottom line, labelled Group B: 5 amber (#E69F00) dots at 4, 7, 10, 13 and 16; under it an amber bracket from 4 to 16 labelled Range = 12.
One reddish purple (#CC79A7) dashed vertical line at 10 crosses both plots, labelled Mean = 10 at its top.
rejection: a number of dots other than 5 in either group
the dashed line at a value other than 10
a range bracket that does not match its group's end dots
images.takeaway: Two groups can share the same mean yet be spread very differently, so describe both the ends and the centre.
images.description: Two dot plots with mean 10: Group A at 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 with range 4, and Group B at 4, 7, 10, 13, 16 with range 12.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask for one careful sentence comparing the groups that mentions both the range and the mean.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap of reading ends and centre helps students write fair comparison statements.
